utility.notes: Banning Electric Utility is the City of Banning's own municipal electric utility, a member of the Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA). Banning is notably absent from SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet, consistent with Banning having its own municipal utility rather than SCE service.

value.name: Banning Electric Utility (BEU)
value.notes: BEU is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Riverside Public Utilities, Burbank Water and Power, and Glendale Water and Power) — it procures and delivers its own power (a mixed portfolio including nuclear, geothermal, solar, landfill gas-to-energy, and hydro, reported 54% renewable in 2021) rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Banning in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Banning Building & Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: The current City Solar Permits page sends the final permit package to the City of Banning Building & Safety division through SmartGov. The Building & Safety page states that the division reviews plans, issues permits and performs inspections. Banning Electric remains the utility/interconnection authority, not the building-permit authority.

permit_url.notes: Current City solar-permit page. It lists a three-step path: plans to Banning Electric, application to Symbium, then stamped/approved plans plus the Symbium-approved application to Building & Safety through SmartGov.

interconnection_url.notes: Banning Electric Utility remains the utility/interconnection authority. The current City Solar Permits page says plans go to Banning Electric first, before Symbium and the Building & Safety permit submission. The BEU Program Guidelines say the utility application review can take up to 45 days and its plan check up to a further 45 days. Those are utility stages, not City permit review time. The same guidelines list a $500 utility-program contribution in aid of construction ($245 production meter + $255 utility application/plan-check/inspection review) and a $60 minimum for additional utility plan checks/inspections beyond the included set; these are preserved here as interconnection/program context rather than displayed as City permit fees.

value: The Electric Utility MUST be contacted first for inspection, at (951) 922-3260
The Electric Utility inspects the complete PV system (module/inverter placement, disconnects, placarding, production meter socket, back-feed voltage, clearances) against the approved plans

Upon passing, the Electric Utility signs off on the Job Card/Permit and advises City of Banning Building and Safety, at which point the customer/contractor can schedule the City's own Building and Safety inspection
The Job Card/Permit must be onsite at the time of inspection
inspection_steps.notes: Per the City's own 'Residential Self Generating Facility Program - Photovoltaic Systems' guidelines PDF, Section C (Electric Utility Inspection Process).

timeline_days.notes: No City building-permit review timeline is stated in the sources reviewed. The 45 + 45 days in the City's Program Guidelines are Electric Utility stages and are recorded under the interconnection field, not as a permit timeline.

value.program_or_pathway: Banning Electric plan review → Symbium automated residential solar/ESS review → City Building & Safety submission through SmartGov
other_conditions: Current City Solar Permits page lists a three-step permit path: first submit plans to Banning Electric, second submit the application to Symbium, third submit stamped/approved plans and the Symbium-approved application to City Building & Safety through SmartGov
Participant must be a City of Banning electric service customer at the address where service is provided
PV system sized not to exceed 100% of the participant's annual electrical usage; Energy Storage Systems sized according to the PV system
A City-owned Production Meter is required to monitor system production, at the participant's/contractor's cost

eligibility_constraints.notes: Current permit path refreshed from the City's Solar Permits page; utility sizing/meter conditions remain from the BEU program guidelines.

permit_fees.notes: City Building & Safety solar permit fees were not verified in the sources reviewed. BEU's $500 contribution in aid of construction and additional utility review charges belong to the utility/interconnection program and are kept under interconnection context rather than displayed as City permit fees.
